blocks.text: 1. BERT

blocks.alt: Input text goes through a BERT encoder stack to produce contextual embeddings

blocks.text: Encoder-Decoder Models, the previous topic, kept both halves of the Transformer for tasks needing both understanding and generation. BERT is a complete, dedicated look at the most influential encoder-only model, explored throughout this topic.

Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers works by pre-training deeply, then adapting per task, a genuinely landmark, widely influential architecture covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Preview

This connects back to a preview of BERT, already covered in Encoder-Only Models. BERT was genuinely introduced there as the single most influential encoder-only model, briefly described in that earlier topic.
This topic genuinely gives it the complete, dedicated treatment already promised, exploring every detail already hinted at generally in that earlier topic.
3. Masked Language Modeling

blocks.alt: Input tokens have some masked, then BERT predicts the masked tokens

blocks.text: BERT's genuinely core training innovation connects back to next-token prediction, already covered in Decoder-Only Models. BERT genuinely masks random words and trains the model to genuinely predict them from surrounding context.
This is a genuinely different training objective than next-token prediction already covered there, a genuinely distinctive approach explored throughout the rest of this topic.
4. Why Masking Rather Than Next-Token Prediction

blocks.alt: Next-token prediction is compared against masked language modeling

blocks.text: This connects back to bidirectional context, already covered in Encoder-Only Models. Next-token prediction, already covered there in Decoder-Only Models, genuinely only uses context from one direction.
Masking genuinely lets BERT use genuinely both directions at once, exploiting its own bidirectional strength, already covered as a defining property of encoder-only architectures.

blocks.text: 5. Pre-Train, Then Fine-Tune
This connects forward to Transfer Learning, covered later in this course. BERT genuinely trains once on a genuinely enormous amount of text, then gets adapted to specific, genuinely different tasks.
This is a genuinely two-stage process explored in complete depth in that later module, a genuinely foundational pattern that BERT helped popularize throughout the field.
6. Next Sentence Prediction

blocks.alt: Sentence A and sentence B are checked for whether B is the next sentence

blocks.text: A genuinely second, complementary training objective connects back to context-aware representations, already covered in Self-Attention. BERT genuinely also learns to predict whether two genuinely given sentences naturally follow each other.

This genuinely second objective, already covered in this section, helps BERT learn genuinely sentence-level relationships, complementing the word-level understanding already covered as Masked Language Modeling.

blocks.content: This combination of Masked Language Modeling and Next Sentence Prediction, both already covered in this topic, together gave BERT its own genuinely rich understanding at both the word level and the sentence level.

blocks.text: 7. Special Tokens

blocks.alt: A CLS token and a SEP token are examples of special tokens

blocks.text: This connects back to Embeddings, already covered in the Transformers module. BERT genuinely uses special marker tokens, like one marking the genuinely start of input and another separating sentences.

This directly extends the embedding vocabulary already covered there with these genuinely structural markers, giving the model genuinely explicit signals about input structure beyond just the words themselves.
8. Fine-Tuning For Classification

blocks.alt: A pretrained BERT gets a classification head added to become a fine-tuned model

blocks.text: This connects back to adding a classification head, already covered in Encoder-Only Models. After pre-training, already covered in this topic, a genuinely small task-specific head gets added and fine-tuned.

This directly reuses the classification head idea already covered there for genuinely many different downstream tasks, letting one single pre-trained BERT model adapt to genuinely many different applications.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing Why BERT Is Genuinely Such A Landmark Model

blocks.alt: Needing deep bidirectional understanding points toward using BERT

blocks.text: This connects back to needing genuinely deep, bidirectional text understanding. BERT's own masked language modeling, already covered in this topic, directly delivers exactly that.

Wanting a genuinely strong, pre-trained starting point for many, genuinely different downstream tasks is another genuine case where BERT's own pre-train-then-fine-tune approach, already covered, directly provides this.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates Masked Language Modeling's own core mechanism, masking a word and predicting it from surrounding bidirectional context, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
sentence = ["the", "cat", "sat", "on", "the", "mat"]
mask_position = 2  # already covered as Masked Language Modeling in this topic

masked_sentence = sentence.copy()
masked_sentence[mask_position] = "[MASK]"  # already covered as special tokens in this topic

print(f"Original sentence: {' '.join(sentence)}")
print(f"Masked sentence: {' '.join(masked_sentence)}")

# already covered as why masking rather than next-token prediction in this topic
left_context = sentence[:mask_position]
right_context = sentence[mask_position + 1:]
print(f"\nLeft context (before the mask): {left_context}")
print(f"Right context (after the mask): {right_context}")
print("BERT genuinely uses both contexts simultaneously, already covered as bidirectional context in this topic")

vocabulary = ["sat", "ran", "jumped", "slept"]
predicted_probabilities = rng.dirichlet(np.ones(len(vocabulary)))
for word, prob in zip(vocabulary, predicted_probabilities):
    print(f"  P('{word}' | context) = {prob:.3f}")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows both the left and right context genuinely available simultaneously for predicting the masked word, exactly the bidirectional advantage already covered as this topic's own core training innovation.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: BERT, Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, is pre-trained deeply, then adapted per task.
Its core training innovation masks random words and predicts them from surrounding context.
Masking lets BERT use both directions of context at once, unlike next-token prediction.
It trains once on enormous text, then gets fine-tuned for specific, different tasks.
A second training objective, Next Sentence Prediction, teaches sentence-level relationships.
Special marker tokens signal structural information beyond just the words themselves.
A small task-specific head gets added and fine-tuned after pre-training.
It delivers genuinely deep, bidirectional text understanding.
